Can Trump be a scam? Absolutely. The guy is basically a professional con-man. But that doesn't necessarily mean that he can't be a professional con-man looking to use his skills for the greater good of the country. Really, I don't think there ist much reason to not trust Trump at his word that his intention is to help the country. Let's break down his motivations:

Money - Doesn't make any sense. The president is not paid well, and Trump already has enough name recognition publicly, and enough power privately, that becoming the President will not help him acquire greater wealth for himself or his family. Realistically, his brutal style of politics has thus far hurt his relations with a number of powerful people and the public as a whole (more on this later).

Power - Anyone who understands power knows that you will hold far more power by pulling strings in the shadows than by stepping out into the spotlight. No one really looked that closely into Trump's political connections before, or the kind of political pull that he had. Now, he is in the spotlight, and everything he says and does will be picked apart and examined under a microscope. With the number of enemies he has made with his political style, nothing will go un-examined or will be forgiven (again, more on this later).

Name Recognition - Many people say that Trump is running just to plaster his name over the White House, so to speak. Based on his personality and past behavior, this isn't really a crazy accusation and may be his core motivation. However, he probably wouldn't be running for greater name recognition, which he has enough of, but to establish the "Trump Legacy". But at the moment, once again, his style of politics has dragged his name through the mud (more on this following).

Truthfully, the only way for Trump to gain money, power, or name recognition from this venture (assuming some combination of those is his goal) is to do a damn good job as president. If he doesn't, he will further infuriate a public that already hates him and cause powerful people to continue to distance themselves from him and actively attack him. And while he has managed to capitalize on attacks from the powerful thus far, it is only because he has managed to appeal to the public directly (and only a small portion of the public at that). In order to remain immune from attacks from the powerful, and to continue to force them to play his game, he will have to appeal to the broader populace and keep them happy. Otherwise, he will be effectively ostracized from American public life.

So, even if his motivations aren't the best, he's really forced into "doing well by the people" so to speak. With that being said, I do believe he is genuine when he says that he is running to help the country. For one, as much as the media and others attack him for flip-flopping on issues, he has actually been very consistent on a key number of issues (i.e., foreign policy and taxation) not only throughout his campaign but throughout most of his life. Whether you agree with Trump about what is best for the country I think it's hard to argue that he isn't doing what he thinks is best for the country (like, say, Bernie Sanders or Ron Paul).
